page: Microsoft Azure E2ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. Hardware cache distribution comprises 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning sits at 16.0 GB total, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It features no local ephemeral storage and does not include hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-threaded performance alongside limitations inherent to a low-core count footprint. Single-thread processing registers average capabilities, shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 2074.09, a Geekbench single-core score of 1673.0, and a strong gzip compression result of 33.06 GB/sec. Conversely, overall compute throughput reflects its 2-vCPU sizing, yielding weak to poor results across multi-core tests such as Geekbench multi-core (3079.0) and PassMark CPU (2015.09). Memory throughput achieves 45.94 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and an average PassMark memory score of 2521.75, though large-block write operations are limited to 21.02 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency and architectural standpoint, the ARM-based E2ps_v6 provides an economical entry point for memory-heavy setups that require substantial RAM per thread without incurring the expense of high vCPU counts. Because local disk storage is absent, all persistent data storage must be mapped to external network volumes, making system architecture dependent on remote block performance. Workloads best aligned with the E2ps_v6 include caching layers like Redis, intermediate data buffers, small-to-midsize in-memory databases, and memory-intensive lightweight microservices.

Equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a high 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio supported by 128 MB of L3 cache. It contains no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote network volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark data demonstrates capable single-thread throughput, highlighted by 33.06 GB/sec in gzip compression and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1673.0, though parallel compute throughput is restricted by the dual-core boundary. Delivering cost-effective memory density without paying for unneeded CPU scale, the E2ps_v6 is suited for in-memory caching platforms, lightweight databases, and memory-heavy application runtimes.
